classes.purpose: Understand and organize an advisory engagement
classes.content: Client and project labels; objectives and audience; company, participant and stakeholder identities; source documents, decks, spreadsheets, notes, transcripts, recordings, dates, facts, financial or operating data, constraints, risks, and open questions

classes.purpose: Weigh evidence and prepare decision-ready advice
classes.content: Material summaries, evidence maps, source limitations, consultant and advisor judgement, Codex inferences, contradictions, hypotheses, options, recommendations, implementation conditions, pending inclusion decisions, case issues, and pseudonymous but linkable audit metadata such as exact source digests, byte counts, stable IDs, dates, counts, and cross-receipt hashes

classes.purpose: Draft and review workpapers, briefs, decks, memos, and decision packs
classes.content: Narrative, charts, claims, citations, speaker notes, review findings, approved content, and final deliverables

boundaries_beyond_codex.destination: Public or otherwise authorized external sources selected for the engagement
boundaries_beyond_codex.purpose: Obtain current industry, market, governance, legal, or other external context relevant to the advisory question
boundaries_beyond_codex.content: Research questions, search terms, selected URLs, retrieved public material, and concise source takeaways; queries may reflect engagement facts when Codex uses them
controls: Use public or authorized sources only.
Do not copy proprietary case material into a public research source or shared playbook.

boundaries_beyond_codex.destination: Mparanza Hosted Voice and its configured realtime/transcription provider
boundaries_beyond_codex.purpose: Capture or upload a spoken debrief and return a transcript bundle
boundaries_beyond_codex.content: Compact case context when enabled, live or uploaded recording content, source metadata, transcript, and media metadata
controls: Hosted Voice is used only after the user selects a voice capture or upload route.
The separate hosted-service record states the source-backed access and retention position.

boundaries_beyond_codex.purpose: Transmit a technical problem or improvement suggestion to the developer and check its status
boundaries_beyond_codex.content: The exact sanitized request approved by the user, plugin name and version, request kind, idempotency metadata, and later receipt identifiers and status tokens
controls: Clara's host-specific instructions require the assistant to show and sanitize the exact submission before invoking the helper; the helper enforces the required bounded diagnostic schema for problems but cannot detect personal data.
The skill instructs Codex to exclude client, source, case, credential, secret, and identifying material.
The skill requires separate consent for problem reports, follow-up evidence, and suggestions; the command-line helper cannot prove that consent occurred.
Claude Cowork stores opaque receipts under its user-scoped plugin data directory and polls them with a trusted SessionStart hook.

boundaries_beyond_codex.purpose: Notify the user when a newer Clara version is published
boundaries_beyond_codex.content: A GET request with a fixed update-check User-Agent; no case files, prompts, transcripts, or client content are included by the plugin
controls: The request uses a fixed HTTPS manifest URL and a three-second timeout.
The check is rate-limited locally and fails open without blocking Clara.
This custom update check is included only in the OpenAI package, not the Claude Cowork package.

boundaries_beyond_codex.purpose: Install Clara's exact declared Python dependencies into the user-scoped Cowork plugin data directory when the fingerprinted dependency cache is absent or invalid
boundaries_beyond_codex.content: Declared package names and version constraints from Clara requirements files, plus ordinary package-index request metadata; no user files, prompts, case data, or advisory content are sent
controls: The trusted SessionStart hook installs only requirements declared in the published Clara package.
Dependencies are installed into Clara's user-scoped plugin data directory rather than the plugin source or connected case folder.
The bootstrap validates imports after installation, uses a requirements fingerprint for reuse, and fails open to file-based work.

boundaries_beyond_codex.purpose: Install the optional shared PaddleOCR runtime after the user approves the roughly 500 MB first-use download
boundaries_beyond_codex.content: Declared OCR package names and version constraints from Clara's published requirements-ocr.txt, plus ordinary package-index request metadata; no user files, document contents, prompts, case data, or advisory content are sent
controls: The input preflight requests this setup only for images or visual-only PDFs that require local OCR.
The Clara skill requires explicit user approval before the managed installer runs.
The installer uses only the published OCR requirements and writes to a fingerprinted user-scoped runtime shared with Vera.

security_controls.control: M6 receipts and sanitized summaries are treated as confidential, pseudonymous, linkable metadata; they remain outside the plugin and source repository by default, and any retention exception requires review of the exact metadata, access, and retention boundary.

M6 raw workbooks and row- or account-level prepared outputs remain in an owner-only private pilot root at a fixed opaque source locator; group/other permission bits and macOS extended ACLs are rejected at audit validation. They are not committed, packaged, or published. Ordinary model processing remains within the user-selected Codex account and this workflow adds no separate external recipient.
